12834.subject: Literature in English
12834.question_text:
'Symbol of fruitfulness, symbol of barrenness Mother and destroyer, the calm and the storm!
Life and desire and dreams and death
Frank Collymore, Hymn to the Sea,

The address to the sea in the lines above is done by the use of
12834.explanation: An apostrophe is a figure of speech in which a speaker directly addresses someone or something that is not present or is an abstract concept, often treating it as though it were a person. In the given lines, the speaker addresses the sea directly, referring to it as a "symbol of fruitfulness," "barrenness," "Mother," "destroyer," and other qualities. The sea is personified and spoken to as if it can hear and respond.

12836.subject: Literature in English
12836.question_text:
'When he gave me the bottle, and I opened it, I was shocked by the odour that hit my nose.
I immediately corked it again, and spat on the floor.'
Isidore Okpewho, The Last Duty.

The reaction in the passage above is that of
12836.explanation: The strong negative response to the odour, immediately corking the bottle, and spitting on the floor suggests a physical reaction of disgust or nausea to the smell.

12837.subject: Literature in English
12837.question_text:
'CYCLIST gets down and begins to prop his bicycle,
CYCLIST: All right. If you're sure it won't take long.
BARBER: I am known for my lightning clippers Even the soldiers know me. I can shave the head of an entire battalion between one coup and the next.
sit down and relax your back. Cycling is not easy when you've abandoned it for some time...
Wole Soyinka, The Beautification of Area Boy.

The literary devices in the dialogue above are
12837.explanation: Hyperbole is an exaggerated statement that is not meant to be taken literally. In the dialogue, the Barber says, "I can shave the head of an entire battalion between one coup and the next." This is clearly an exaggeration to emphasize the speed at which he works. Allusion is a reference to something outside the immediate text. The Barber gives a famous reference to the era when coups succeeded one another in Nigeria's history.

12838.subject: Literature in English
12838.question_text:
'For seven days it rained that June;
A storm half out to sea kept turning around like a dog trying to settle himself on a rug; We were the fleas that complained in his hair.'
John Updike, Wash

The images set in the lines above are of
12838.explanation: The passage uses vivid imagery to convey a sense of discomfort and a looming threat of destruction. The storm "kept turning around like a dog trying to settle himself on a rug," which suggests the storm's restlessness and chaotic nature. Additionally, the comparison of people to "fleas that complained in his hair" evokes a sense of irritation and helplessness in the face of a powerful and uncontrollable force (the storm).

12839.subject: Literature in English
12839.question_text:
'We have been asleep, Mr. Speaker, my fellow citizens; asleep in our dream of security! Asleep in our well-meaning, sportsmanlike way of wishing the other fellow well. Asleep in the false security of accepting all men of goodwill who would be free as men of honor.'
Ralph Ellison, Juneteenth.

The force of the speech above is sustained on.
12839.explanation: In the passage, the phrase "asleep" is repeated multiple times to emphasise the speaker's point. This repetition creates a rhythmic, almost hypnotic effect, reinforcing the idea that society has been complacent or unaware of the real dangers or challenges. The repeated use of "asleep" helps to underline the speaker's urgency and frustration, making the speech more powerful and impactful.

12841.subject: Literature in English
12841.question_text:
'Thomas Gradgrind, sir. A man who proceeds upon the principle that two is not to be talked into allowing for anything over.'
Charles Dickens, Hard Times

From the passage above, Thomas Gradgrind is
12841.explanation: Dogmatic refers to someone who strongly adheres to a set of principles and is unwilling to consider any alternatives or deviations. In the passage, Thomas Gradgrind is described as a person who strictly follows rigid principles (in this case, mathematical precision), implying he is inflexible in his thinking.

12842.subject: Literature in English
12842.question_text:
'Jose Palacios, his oldest servant, found him floating naked with his eyes open in the purifying waters of his bath and thought he had drowned.
He knew this was one of the many ways the General meditated, but the ecstasy in which he lay drifting seemed that of a man no longer of this world.'
Gabriel Garcia Marquez, The General in His Labyrinth.

The master in the passage above is obviously in a state of
12842.explanation: The passage describes the master floating naked in the bath with his eyes open, showing signs of meditative ecstasy and drifting, which are indicative of a trance-like state where the person is deeply absorbed or lost in thoughts or sensations. This state is further emphasized by the description of the ecstasy in which the master is lying, suggesting a detachment from the physical world and a heightened state of consciousness or meditation.

12843.subject: Literature in English
12843.question_text: The character 'boy' is used alongside 'the old Man' in the novel to demonstrate.
12843.explanation: In The Old Man and the Sea, the character of the boy is a contrast to the old man (Santiago) and symbolizes both the old man's past vitality and the reality of his current situation. The relationship between Santiago and the boy illustrates the failing productivity that accompanies old age because Santiago is no longer able to provide for himself or catch fish as he once did.

options.text: the humiliation that is in old age
different types of characters in the story
the failing productivity that accompanies old age

12844.subject: Literature in English
12844.question_text: The skeleton of the marlin implies the
12844.explanation: In The Old Man and the Sea, the skeleton of the marlin symbolises the futility of human struggle. Santiago's heroic battle to catch the fish and his ultimate defeat by the sharks demonstrate the fleeting nature of success and the inevitability of loss, despite one's best efforts. The marlin's skeleton, once beautiful and strong, now remains a symbol of Santiago's failed attempt to preserve his victory.

12845.subject: Literature in English
12845.question_text: The Old Man and the Sea epitomises
12845.explanation: The Old Man and the Sea is seen as a story about the human struggle against nature, symbolized by Santiago's battle with the marlin. While Santiago’s effort and determination are heroic, his ultimate loss of the fish to the sharks suggests the futility and the transient nature of human endeavours.

options.text: the relationship between a man and a fish

12846.subject: Literature in English
12846.question_text: Santiago loses his catch to the sharks because
12846.explanation: In The Old Man and the Sea, Santiago catches a giant marlin, but during his struggle to bring it in, the fish is wounded. The blood from the marlin attracts sharks, which eventually attack the fish. Despite Santiago’s efforts to fend off the sharks, they devour the marlin, leaving Santiago with little to show for his efforts.

options.text: he does not sail home early

12849.subject: Literature in English
12849.question_text: Laye's stay with Uncle Mamadou reveals a lot about
12849.explanation: In The African Child, Camara Laye's stay with Uncle Mamadou showcases the traditional African practice of communal living, where extended families and the community play an important role in raising children.

options.text: his unwillingness to stay with his parents
the strength of communal living in Africa

12850.subject: Literature in English
12850.question_text: The setting of The African Child is a kingdom with
12850.explanation: In The African Child by Camara Laye, the setting of the story reflects a combination of Islamic culture and the influences of modernity. The story is set in a traditional and predominantly agrarian community undergoing influences from Islam and France.

12851.subject: Literature in English
12851.explanation: In The African Child, Camara Laye uses a first-person narrative technique, where the protagonist recounts his experiences directly. This approach provides an intimate perspective, allowing readers to connect with the character's personal emotions, thoughts and experiences.

options.text: quickens the tempo of his narrative

12852.subject: Literature in English
12852.question_text: Pa Noble became a living legend because
12852.explanation: In Second Class Citizen by Buchi Emecheta, Pa Noble is a character surrounded by various stories, some of which are exaggerated or conflicted. These stories, along with his larger-than-life image, contribute to his status as a "living legend." The different narratives about him, which blend fact with fiction, elevate his reputation in the community, making him more than just a man, but a legendary figure.

options.text: several conflicting stories were woven around him
he attained the status of a first-class citizen
he was the only successful son of a Benin chief
he was rich and very generous

12853.subject: Literature in English
12853.question_text: The marriage of Adah and Francis collapses because of
12853.explanation: The collapse of Adah and Francis's marriage is primarily due to external pressures on the couple. Throughout the novel,  Adah and Francis face numerous challenges and obstacles that put a strain on their relationship. These external pressures include societal expectations, financial difficulties, and the impact of cultural and racial discrimination. These factors contribute to the breakdown of their marriage and this highlights the influence of external forces on their personal lives and relationship.

12854.subject: Literature in English
12854.question_text: The character of Marshal in the play shows that
12854.explanation: In Morountodun, the character of Marshal represents the pursuit of power. Throughout the play, Marshal's actions and motivations reveal a deep desire for control and influence, particularly over others. His character is driven by the need for power, which influences his decisions and his relationships with other characters.

12855.subject: Literature in English
12855.question_text: The sub-plots of the play are united by
12855.explanation: In Morountodun, the various sub-plots are united by their focus on the central character, Morountodun. These sub-plots revolve around the heroine's struggles, including her journey, her relationships and the larger societal issues she faces. The attention to her character ties together the different threads of the play, making her the central figure around which the action and various conflicts unfold.

options.text: a common concern for the heroine

12857.subject: Literature in English
12857.question_text: The war in Femi Osofisan's Morountondun symbolizes the struggle between the
12857.explanation: In Morountodun by Femi Osofisan, the war symbolizes a broader societal struggle between the ruling class (bourgeoisie) and the working class (proletariat). This conflict is evident in the play, where the exploitation and oppression of the working class by those in power are central themes.

12859.subject: Literature in English
12859.question_text: The frequent intervention of the Director makes the stage experience of Morountodun very
12859.explanation: In Morountodun, the director’s frequent interventions serve to break the traditional boundaries of a stage performance, making the experience less formal and more interactive.

12864.subject: Literature in English
12864.question_text:
Not yet old enough for a man, nor young enough for a boy; as a squash is before 't is almost an apple; 't is with him in standing water, between boy and man. He is very well-favoured, and he speaks very shrewishly; one would think his mother's milk were scarce out of him.

The images in the quotation above express the speaker's
12864.explanation: In this passage from Twelfth Night, the speaker (Feste) describes someone who is in the awkward phase between childhood and adulthood. The use of "squash" and "codling" (unripe fruits) as metaphors highlights how the person is neither fully a boy nor a man. The speaker's comment on the person's "shrewish" speech and the suggestion that "his mother's milk were scarce out of him" expresses disdain and a lack of respect.

12868.subject: Literature in English
12868.question_text:
Come away, come away, death,
And in sad cypress let me be laid...

In the lines above, the character is
12868.explanation: The lines you refer to are from Feste's song in Twelfth Night, where the character expresses sorrow over love that is not returned. The use of "Come away, come away, death" reflects the speaker's deep despair, wishing for death as an escape from the pain of unrequited love. The mention of being laid in "sad cypress," a tree often associated with mourning, reinforces the theme of sadness and loss, rather than a preference for death itself or a cypress coffin.

options.text: expressing his preference for a cypress coffin

12876.subject: Literature in English
12876.question_text:
Duke:
Be clamorous, and leap all civil bounds,
Rather than make unprofited return.

Duke's statement above to Cesario means that he should
12876.explanation: In this line, the Duke is urging Cesario (Viola in disguise) to take bold action in his pursuit of Olivia. The phrase "be clamorous" suggests making a loud or forceful approach to capture Olivia's attention, and "leap all civil bounds" implies disregarding social norms or restrictions in order to achieve the goal. Therefore, the Duke is encouraging Cesario to be conspicuous and assertive in a way that will ensure Olivia notices him, even if it means disregarding conventional social boundaries.

options.text: jump the fence to see Olivia
shout to be seen and heard by Olivia
fortify himself against any denial to see Olivia

12878.subject: Literature in English
12878.question_text: The traditional verse form of speech as dialogue in Twelfth Night is used to symbolize the
12878.explanation: In Twelfth Night, Shakespeare uses verse (typically iambic pentameter) for more elevated, serious or formal moments, often when characters like Orsino or Viola speak. Prose is used for more casual, comedic, or lower-class characters (like Sir Toby or Feste). This distinction helps to highlight differences in social class of the characters.

options.text: function of poetry in the play

12881.subject: Literature in English
12881.question_text: Twelfth Night is preoccupied with the juxtaposition of
12881.explanation: Twelfth Night explores the theme of appearance versus reality, where characters often disguise themselves, leading to confusion and mistaken identities. This theme runs throughout the play, particularly in the cases of Viola and Cesario, and the humorous situations that arise from the characters' misperceptions and misunderstandings.

12885.subject: Literature in English
12885.question_text: In Niyi Osundare' s ' They Too Are The Earth', the musical effect is achieved by
12885.explanation: Repetition is a key technique used by Osundare in this poem to create rhythm and musicality. The repeated use of words or phrases enhances the poem's musicality and places emphasis on the parts of the poem that convey the theme.

12886.subject: Literature in English
12886.question_text: The rhyming pattern in the last stanza of Okigbo' s Hurrah for Thunder' makes the stanza
12886.explanation: The last stanza of Okigbo's "Hurrah for Thunder" is a couplet. A Couplet is a pair of lines that usually rhyme.

12887.subject: Literature in English
12887.question_text: In Keats ' Ode on a Grecian Urn', the recurrent use of the rhetorical question in the lines above suggests
12887.explanation: In Keats' Ode on a Grecian Urn, the recurrent use of the rhetorical question in the lines above suggests admiration and amazement. The rhetorical questions in the poem are used by the speaker to reflect on the timeless beauty and mystery of the scenes depicted on the urn. These questions express the speaker's awe and fascination with the urn's ability to capture eternal moments, frozen in time.

12897.subject: Literature in English
12897.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The most important concepts in poetry are
12897.explanation: While elements like plot and character are more prominent in narrative forms like fiction or drama, poetry relies heavily on rhythm (meter, rhyme, and other sound patterns) and imagery (vivid and descriptive language) to convey emotions, ideas and experiences.

12898.subject: Literature in English
12898.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The literary device which anticipates that an event will take place is best described as
12898.explanation: Foreshadowing is a technique used by writers to give hints or clues about what will happen later in the story. It helps build suspense and prepares the audience for upcoming events.

12899.subject: Literature in English
12899.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The flat character in a literary work
12899.explanation: A flat character is a simple, one-dimensional character who embodies a single trait, quality or idea. Such characters do not undergo significant development or growth throughout the story. They are often used to support the plot or highlight aspects of more complex characters.

options.text: is the same as the round character
cannot be found in an allegory

12902.subject: Literature in English
12902.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The overwhelming pride that destroys the tragic hero is called
12902.explanation: Hubris refers to excessive pride or arrogance in a character, often a tragic hero, which leads to their downfall. This concept is a hallmark of classical tragedy, where the hero's inability to recognise their flaws or limitations causes catastrophic consequences.

12904.subject: Literature in English
12904.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

A farce refers to a drama that has elements of the
12904.explanation: A farce is a type of comedy that uses exaggerated and absurd situations, improbable events and physical humour to entertain the audience. It often relies on slapstick, mistaken identities and ridiculous scenarios for comedic effect.

12906.subject: Literature in English
12906.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

Catharsis is experienced
12906.explanation: Catharsis refers to the emotional release or purification (of pity and fear) that the audience experiences at the end of a tragic play, according to Aristotle. It occurs after the dramatic events have unfolded and the resolution is reached, not before or during.

options.text: after one has written a play
when a play is still being staged

12908.subject: Literature in English
12908.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

An extended fictional narrative which is realistic is known as a
12908.explanation: A novel is a long, fictional narrative that explores realistic characters, settings and events and delves deeply into themes and human experiences. A Diary refers to a personal, non-fictional record of daily events and thoughts. A Novella is a shorter fictional narrative than a novel but longer than a short story. A Short story is a brief fictional narrative focusing on a single event or character.

12910.subject: Literature in English
12910.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

The technique in which both the stage and the auditorium are involved in a lay production is called
12910.explanation: Audience participation involves direct interaction with the audience in the auditorium as the play is acted on stage.

12916.subject: Literature in English
12916.question_text: The theme of Browning's My Last Duchess' is
12916.explanation: The Duke, the speaker in the poem, reveals his pride, arrogance and obsessive desire for control as he narrates the story of his late wife. He views her as a possession rather than a person and values her only because of how she reflects on his status and authority. His disdain for her independent expressions of joy and his chilling implications about her fate underscore his hubris and authoritarian nature.

options.text: the pitfalls of a duchess now dead
the pride and arrogance of an aristocrat

12920.subject: Literature in English
12920.question_text: Tanure Ojaide's The Owl Wakes Us portrays a society that is
12920.explanation: In Ojaide’s poem, the presence of the owl and its call awakens us to an impending doom on society due to societal instability.

12921.subject: Literature in English
12921.question_text: In Mapanje's When This Carnival Finally Closes', the poet is describing the
12921.explanation: The poem is a metaphorical commentary on the political situation, where the "carnival" symbolises the chaotic, superficial and corrupt nature of leadership. The speaker reflects on the end of this "carnival" as a moment of reckoning, hinting at the negative effects of sycophancy, exploitation, and misgovernance, which have been prominent throughout the event.

options.text: role of spirits in a carnival
role of drumming and dancing in a carnival
role of sycophancy and bad leadership

12925.subject: Literature in English
12925.question_text: From the tone of Wole Soyinka's 'Telephone Conversation', the two persons talking hold each other in
12925.explanation: The poem explores a telephone conversation between a prospective tenant (the speaker) and a landlady. The landlady's reaction to the speaker's race and her questions reveal a sense of suspicion and prejudice, while the speaker's responses indicate discomfort and unease. Both characters display a lack of trust and understanding towards each other, characterized by mutual suspicion and subtle conflict.

12928.subject: Literature in English
12928.question_text: The major theme of Thomas Gray''s Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'' is that death renders life
12928.explanation: Gray's poem meditates on death and the lives of ordinary people, particularly those buried in the churchyard. It reflects on how death brings equality to all, regardless of social status, and that everyone, whether rich or poor, will eventually face it. The poem suggests that the simple lives of the poor, though uncelebrated, have meaning and dignity in the face of death. It is a reflection on the shared human experience of mortality.

12929.question_text: Browning's My Last Duchess apparently shows the Duke's
12929.explanation: The poem is written to praise Fra Pandolf, the woman he marries because he his displeased by his late wife.

12933.subject: Literature in English
12933.question_text: John Keats' 'Ode on a Grecian Urn' expresses the idea that
12933.explanation: In the poem, Keats reflects on the timeless nature of art, symbolized by the Grecian urn. The urn preserves an image of eternal beauty and perfection, untouched by the passage of time. The idea that "life is long, art is longer" comes from the notion that while human life is fleeting, art—capturing beauty and meaning—endures far beyond the lives of those who create it.

options.text: every work of art is beautiful
life is long, art is longer

12942.subject: Literature in English
12942.question_text:
'The curfew tolls the knell of parting day,
The lowing herd wind slowly o'er the lea,
The plowman homeward plods his weary way;
And leaves the world to darkness and to me.'

In the lines above from Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard', the imagery is
12942.explanation: The imagery in these lines evokes a tranquil rural scene at twilight, where the "curfew tolls" signalling the end of the day, and various elements of the countryside—such as the "lowing herd" and the "plowman homeward"—paint a picture of a peaceful, quiet evening setting. The transition from day to night and the solitude that follows are key components of the imagery. The image of approaching darkness symbolises the advent of death, which is the central theme of the poem.

options.text: of an approaching night in a rustic setting
about a village under a curfew one night
of an approaching death in a village
of a man abandoned in his homeward journey

41536.subject: Literature in English
41536.explanation: In the poem, the night is portrayed as a time when the dangers and challenges faced by the people of Soweto are concealed or obscured, allowing evil or danger to creep unnoticed. The "enemy" refers to the social, political, and possibly physical dangers lurking in the darkness, which the night aids .

41537.subject: Literature in English
41537.question_text: The diction of Femi Osofisan's Morountodun can be described as
41537.explanation: The play addresses societal and political issues, with characters engaging in discussions that reveal the social, cultural and political struggles of the time. The dialogue in Morountodun uses rhetorical devices, persuasive language and impassioned speeches to convey its themes and persuade the audience to reflect on the issues at hand.

41538.subject: Literature in English
41538.question_text:

41539.subject: Literature in English
41539.question_text:

life: though unreal shapes be pictured there,
